headline: How to know if your property is tiny home-ready?
articleBody:
Wondering if your current property is a good fit for a tiny home? It's a common question, and getting it right from the start can save you a lot of time and money. The first big hurdle is understanding your property's zoning and local codes. Zen Tiny Homes has extensive experience working with city and county stakeholders in San Diego and across Southern California, giving us a unique insight into what's permissible. We can help clarify if your tiny home will be considered an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) on a foundation or a mobile unit, as the rules for each vary significantly. Zoning dictates things like setbacks, maximum occupancy, and even what types of structures are allowed.

Next, let's talk about the practical side of your land. We'll look at the topography – is it flat enough, or will extensive grading be needed? Where will your tiny home connect to utilities like water, sewer (or septic), and electricity? We also assess drainage to prevent future issues and consider the optimal foundation setup. Our Site Plan Program specifically covers land use planning, zoning, topography, aerial mapping, and utility access to give you a complete picture. 

Finally, access for construction and delivery is crucial. Can a crane get in if needed? Is there enough space for our team to work safely? And don't forget the 'soft' elements like how a tiny home will fit with your existing property layout and your personal lifestyle goals. It’s about more than just fitting the structure; it’s about creating a cohesive, livable space. A professional site feasibility consultation from Zen Tiny Homes can pinpoint all these factors and ensure your property is truly tiny home-ready.
